- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Backport #8230 to `core_r0.20.0` so MFSDP v2 can save and resume expert-parallel MoE checkpoints. Previously, a BF16 EP=2 run could train successfully but fail at its first save with `NotImplementedError: MFSDP v2 optimizer checkpointing does not support expert parallelism yet`. Loading now also refreshes compute weights from restored main weights before the next forward.

Two source commits are cherry-picked without content conflicts or release-specific code changes:

- #8230: `db3a6cd8a03eb550e9fa4532a0db96778bb56fc5` — checkpoint fix and regression tests.
- #8326: `74c9420e35cc3c1226e53421f5ff718653aa8399` — required test setup/teardown follow-up. With #8230 alone, running its EP checkpoint test first reproduces `Backend can not be changed after use` in the next expert-parallel test. This follow-up selects the backend through the shared fixture and clears cached DTensor meshes before destroying groups.

The release already contains the required runtime APIs. No other main-branch changes are included. Independent review of the complete release diff found no remaining actionable code issues.

## Validation

On two RTX 6000 Ada GPUs, PyTorch `2.13.0a0+8145d630e8.nv26.06`, Transformer Engine `2.17.1+4329ff84`:

- Checkpoint, optimizer-checkpoint, expert-parallel, annotation, and DBuffer files: **61 passed, 37 skipped per rank**.
- EP-first ordering that failed before #8326: **50 passed, 37 skipped per rank** after including it.
- `BASE_REF=core_r0.20.0 CHECK_ONLY=true SKIP_DOCS=false bash tools/autoformat.sh`: Black, isort, Pylint, and Ruff passed. Its nonblocking mypy step reports 19 annotation errors in two files; the release versions of those files also report 19, with an added diagnostic on `finish_grad_sync()` replacing one in the removed helper.
- `git diff --check` passed. Both commits are signed and include Chen's sign-off.

This exercises the TE <2.18 compatibility path. TE >=2.18, EP=4, EP>1 with expert-DP size greater than one, and end-to-end training were not run locally. Tests requiring additional ranks skip; full CI remains pending.

## Issue tracking

Related to #8230 and #8326.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests (backported upstream coverage)
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.
